reason: Misspelling of falcate (sickle-shaped acumen); falcate is a synonym of PATO_0002215 falciform.
Gibberulous is the diminutive of gibbous (slightly swollen on one side); like 'sub-' it is the same value said loosely, so no separate class.
Girth of a trunk or stem is its circumference; the number goes with it as a bounded measurement (docs/odp/02).
Navicular already maps to scaphoid (rule C214); 'half' (like one side of a boat) has no term and is lost.
Clasping means at least partly surrounding the axis; FLOPO:0991105 sheathing needs a closed tube, so a base that half-sheathes is clasping.
Ill-odoured = having an unpleasant, offensive smell, which is the definition of foetid.
Misspelling of imbricate (overlapping lobes and bracts).
It places vascular bundles between air canals, which makes it a kind of bundle, not a quality. 'Bundle' alone was already rejected as a generic part.

label: polyhedral
definition: A convex 3-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being bounded by several flat or nearly flat faces that meet at sharp angles. NOTE: PATO:0001977 angular is a 2-D outline quality; 'irregularly' (unequal faces) is dropped.
reason: A common way to describe seeds that are packed tightly together. No PATO 3-D term covers flat faces with sharp angles.

There is no general term for an apiculus: PO has only the palea and lemma ones, 'apiculum' was rejected as a generic part, and PATO lists apiculate only under sharpness. Mapping it to 'not mucronate' would be doubtful.
Same as lenticellate (rule C204): bearing lenticels.
Liver colour is a dark reddish brown, which is red and brown hue at low brightness.
'2-3 loculate' counts locules (PO_0025263 locule). The anther example is a fragment about where the locules sit.
A shape between two values, obovate (PATO_0001936) and spatulate (PATO_0001937); 'narrowly' is a modifier.
Transcription fragment of 'narrowly triangular to linear...'; not a word.
Channelled maps to grooved (rule C195); this is its negation.
Negation of PATO_0002274 mottled.
Negation of PATO_0000963 opaque, about scale cells.
Negation of FLOPO petiolate. 'Not truly petiolate' can mean pseudopetiolate, so the negation is safer than sessile (PATO_0001436).
A branch that does not branch again lacks branches: PATO_0000414 unbranched.
There is no positive term to negate. Thicket-forming describes how the plant grows in a population, not a quality worth a class for 2 statements.
A chemical content, not a form quality, with no PATO term. A doubtful class for 2 statements.
Two shape values joined: ovoid (PATO_0001891, synonym ovoid) and pyramidal (PATO_0002336). Treat as a continuum, not a new term.
A loose likeness for tiers of spreading branches or flowers. It is used for both inflorescence and branching and is too vague for a class.
Styles or sepals joined to each other are like parts fused: connate. 'Partially' is a degree that stays in the record.
A sweet, fruity, pleasant smell; the peach comparison is kept as the cue.
It states that the seed tip carries a peg, a generic part with no PO class. PATO_0002535 peg-like is the shape of the whole bearer, not of its tip.
The pulp may be an aril, a sarcotesta or the fruit flesh; which part is present cannot be told from the text. 'Covered' was rejected before (C240).
A likeness to a plant group that mixes shape (terete, slender) with stiffness and habit. No single quality can be read from it.
Saw-like teeth point forward like those of a saw, which is serrate.
